subject: Hosting choice & security clarifications — MediCore HIPAA needs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@medicorehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting choice & security clarifications — MediCore HIPAA needs

Hi Emily / Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clarity around your use case and security requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap from discovery:
- Primary workload: extracting structured outputs from clinical notes and generating patient-facing summaries.
- Regulatory: must be HIPAA-covered; PHI cannot leave your VPC without contractual and technical safeguards.
- Desired timeframe: pilot in Q3, production in Q4 (procurement window late July).
- Cost sensitivity: need to understand unit economics for private vs dedicated.

Security requirements called out on the call:
- Signed BAA (required before any PHI handling).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short list of audit artifacts (control descriptions, penetration test summary, change management logs).
- Option to host in a Private deployment (VPC) or fully on-premises if required by procurement.

Our initial recommendation (high level):
- For pilot: Redwood Dedicated with customer VPC peering + KMS integrations can meet most timelines and gives isolation without full on-prem lift.
- For long-term/regulatory strictness: Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package) — supports KMS/HSM and air-gap patterns.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) We’ll send the SOC 2 digest and a HIPAA deployment matrix (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Rishi to walk through network diagrams, KMS options, and audit evidence (availability next week: Tue/Wed).
3) Share your procurement contact so we can kick off the BAA and draft SOW.

Attachments: HIPAA-deployment-matrix.xlsx (summary of options & impact), high-level SOC2 digest (will send in follow-up from SE).

If any of the recap items are off, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise, Rishi — can you pick two slots for next week?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Hosting choice & security clarifications — MediCore HIPAA needs

Thanks Sofia — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Preference: our security team strongly prefers Private VPC for any PHI workload. Open to Dedicated for a timeboxed pilot if the BAA and technical isolation meet our controls, but we need written confirmation on customer-managed keys (BYOK) and no shared GPU tenancy.
2) On-premises: we are evaluating — can you confirm whether Redwood’s on-prem package supports air-gapped deployment with no outbound telemetry? Our infosec will ask for that.
3) SOC 2: we need the Type II report (redacted is fine) and a list of the artifacts you can provide for vendor assessment (pen test, change management, user access reviews).
4) Timeline: procurement needs at least a 6-8 week window after receiving commercial and security artifacts.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire (excerpt) — the procurement team will fill the commercial section once we have a BAA draft.

Best,
Emily Chen
Director of IT Security, MediCore Health
emily.chen@medicorehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2222

Hi Emily — quick technical follow-up with concrete answers and options. Long but wanted to be explicit for your InfoSec/procurement review.

Short answers first: 
- BAA: yes, Redwood will sign a BAA. We’ll provide a standard BAA draft for review and can iterate.
- SOC 2 Type II: we can provide the redacted report and a control mapping package (list of artifacts and evidence samples).
- BYOK / KMS: Supported across Dedicated and Private. Private on-prem supports HSM integrations for key custody.
- Telemetry / outbound: Private on-prem can be deployed in air-gapped mode with telemetry disabled. The VPC option limits egress; dedicated hosted still has managed control plane traffic (we can enumerate endpoints to allow-list).

Detailed breakdown of deployment modes and compliance fit: 
1) Hosted API (redwood.ai endpoint) — NOT recommended for PHI unless precertified with an enterprise BAA and dedicated tenancy + strict contract controls. Even then, some customers prefer not to send PHI to a shared control plane.

2) Redwood Dedicated — Good middle ground for pilots. Provides isolated GPU pools, private networking (VPC peering), and BYOK. Faster to stand up than full Private on-prem. Suitable if procurement allows 3rd-party managed infra with contractual assurances.

3) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) — Best fit for strict HIPAA controls. Offers customer-controlled networking, optional on-prem air-gap, HSM/KMS integrations, and can be configured for minimal outbound telemetry. Longer lead time and higher engineering coordination but meets the tightest audit requirements.

Attachments I’m dropping here: 
- redwood_soc2-summary.pdf (redacted Type II + control mapping)
- HIPAA-deployment-matrix.xlsx (detailed comparison of configuration options against your questionnaire)

Proposed next steps (technical): 
- 60-min session: deep dive on network diagram and KMS flow. My availability Wed 06/17 10:00-11:30 PT or Thu 06/18 09:00-12:00 PT.
- If you want an on-prem air-gap checklist, we can produce one after the technical session.

If helpful I can prepare a short one-page control mapping (how Redwood’s controls map to your questionnaire) before procurement.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
